A fabric of processes, resources and work.
Observe what happens under the assumptions you declare.

Synthetic research · local execution

01 / Declare the system

Research workspace

The same C++ engine runs here through WebAssembly.

production.config.v1

Define resources, labor, capacity, process stages, jobs and risk in JSON. The engine validates the exact text.

Example configuration
Preparing the example…

A general engine

Declare relationships.
Inspect consequences.

ResourcesLaborCapacity
Process stages → Outputs

Dependencies · retained progress · declared risk

Each job instantiates a process. Its stages draw on input stocks and available pools, then produce configured outputs. The timeline emerges from those constraints.

What the model assumes
  • Inputs are consumed together at a feasible stage start. Outputs become available to other stages on the next tick.
  • Pauses retain work already completed. Available labor and capacity reset each tick.
  • FIFO and earliest deadline are greedy scheduling policies. They establish no optimum or fairness claim.
  • Risk probabilities are supplied assumptions and remain uncalibrated. A recorded reason is the first blocking condition.
  • Compensation accrues across the full horizon, including idle time and absence. Payment, funding, viability and governance are not modeled.

Recorded result

The default example runs when this page opens. Editing an input preserves the last completed result until another run finishes.

    02 / Observe the full horizon

    Production observations

    Compensation due is an obligation in declared currency minor units; no decimal scale is inferred. Settlement: not modeled. Completion records do not establish output sufficiency, worker benefit or economic viability.

    Jobs at the end of the horizon
    Job / processReleaseDeadlineCompletionStatusMissed deadline

    Recorded timeline

    Select a tick on the timeline or use the recorded tick controls below.

    ProgressStarted, no progressWaiting to startUnreleasedAlready completed

    Playback reads completed records. It does not rerun the engine or change the horizon.

    Tick detail

    Stage work and the first recorded condition at this tick
    Job / stageWork this tickCompleted / requiredStatusRecorded conditionStart / completion

    Closing resource stock

    Closing stocks at this tick · each resource retains its own unit
    ResourceDeclared unitStock

    Available and used pools

    Pool availability and use at this tick
    Pool / kindDeclared unitAvailableUsedCompensation due
    Events at this tick
    Full horizon resource accounting
    Closing = opening + produced − consumed − lost. Unrealized output is separate from stock loss.
    Resource / unitOpeningProducedConsumedLostClosingUnrealized output
    Validated system inventory and process definitions

    Post-profit-production is a research model. The engine records consequences of declared constraints and synthetic risks; empirical adequacy, consent and compensation settlement require separate work.
